Nina — thanks, great questions. Attached is a draft matrix that maps the marketplace "region" selection to our default processing/storage model across AWS/GCP/Azure (residency_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a draft SLA we typically start negotiations with (marketplace_sla_draft.pdf). High level answers below and next steps at the bottom.

High level:
- Region mapping: For marketplace listings you can choose a region (US/EU/APAC). That choice pins the customer to a preferred deployment (e.g., us-west AWS, europe-west GCP, or west-europe Azure) for model execution and primary storage. We also offer a "secondary DR" region setting — disabled by default for residency-sensitive listings.
- Retention defaults:
  - Runtime KV cache: 24 hours (configurable, down to session-only).
  - Customer content (S3/GCS/Blob object stores): default 90 days; configurable by contract down to 0 days with agreed runbook.
  - Audit logs and telemetry: 365 days by default (can be reduced per-enterprise package).
- Deletion workflow:
  1) Cloudfolio triggers deletion via API or HubSpot workflow (we can accept signed DocuSign request).
  2) Deletion job runs against primary storage and KV caches; objects moved to a secure deletion queue and overwritten per-cloud provider best practices.
  3) We generate an audit record (timestamp, object keys, job id) and provide a signed deletion assertion. For high-assurance needs we can produce a hash list of deleted object IDs and retention of deletion logs for a negotiated window.
- Multi-cloud failover caveat: temporary replication (for replication-based DR) is off by default; if enabled we'll document the secondary location and time-limited replication TTLs. Any replication will be listed in the matrix and must be accepted during onboarding.

Sean / Vanessa — quick technical clarifications to be included in the matrix: 

- Object storage: primary objects (customer artifacts, uploads) live in a customer-specific bucket/container in the chosen cloud region (S3/GCS/Azure Blob). We do not co-mingle customer buckets.
- Model inference: runtime is executed on VMs/containers pinned to the same region; transient KV cache is kept in local ephemeral NVMe or region-local managed Redis.
- Deletion mechanics:
  - Soft-delete stage: objects are marked for deletion and retained in a quarantine bucket for up to the negotiated retention purge window (default 48 hours) to support accidental restores.
  - Final deletion: we trigger a provider-native secure-delete (API call + overwrite per provider where supported). For GCS/Azure where overwrite semantics vary, we perform a two-pass delete + metadata wipe and record the operation id.
- Backups & logs: backups (if enabled) are encrypted and kept per-region; logs are streamed to a customer-dedicated project/tenant and can be routed to your SIEM endpoint.
- Evidence of deletion: we emit a deletion-runbook ID and a signed JSON assertion containing object keys and timestamps. If they need a higher-assurance certified deletion, we can run a cryptographic hash of object contents before deletion and include hash list in the assertion (note: hashes require coordination on retrieval window).

Team — adding legal/regulatory perspective for Cloudfolio's procurement. Main points: 

1) Deletion attestation: procurement typically wants a signed attestation that includes deletion-runbook ID, timestamp, and either the deletion assertion (list of object IDs) or a cryptographic hash bundle. We should offer both options and call out costs/timing for hash generation in the SLA.
2) Retention carve-outs: need clear language describing retention for audit logs vs. customer content; Cloudfolio must be able to choose shorter log retention for PII-sensitive listings.
3) Discovery/Compliance requests: define a 72-hour window for initial acknowledgement of DSGVO/CYBER subpoenas and a 14-day window for response unless legal escalation is required.

I've noted redline comments in marketplace_sla_draft.pdf (see attached). Two asks for engineering: 
- Ben, confirm we can produce the hash bundle within 7 days of request (best-effort) and whether that requires pulling objects into a transient compute env to hash.
- Sean, confirm whether the "no secondary replication" flag can be enforced at listing creation in the marketplace UI (we shouldn't rely solely on ops runbook).
